\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شکستن} (shekastan)}{شکستن (shekastan)}]{\fa{شکستن} (shekastan) — to break}

\label{lesson:FA-C132-shekastan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to jump, then the Persian for to fall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شکستن}}
\textbf{\fa{شکستن}} — \emph{shekastan} — \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shekastan} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed: it continues Middle Persian \emph{škastan}, \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*skeyd-}, \textquotedblleft{}to split\textquotedblright{}, the root of Latin \emph{scindere}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shekastan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to jump, then the Persian for to fall, then say \emph{shekastan} again
\end{itemize}
